what_happened: In job 02gf, the user corrected Athena's first reading of a follow-up request about writing landing records, before work went on. The user kept the earlier decisions: the remote is the source of truth, the local ref moves only after the push succeeds, and a rejected push is rebuilt and retried. They then narrowed the plan in three ways. First, the records writing goes in gh::land_pr behind the records sink it already takes, and is tested through the free function. Second, one small constructor builds the real records sink from a Git and its remote. Athena::land_pr, and so drain.rs, calls it. A test on the constructor must fail if the wiring passes no sink, and there is no fake-runner rig for Athena::land_pr. Third, there is no merge-requested marker. When the merge cannot be confirmed, no landing record is written, a warning names the intent, exit codes stay as they are, and reconcile repairs it later. display.rs changes only if the warning needs one line. The event does not say what the first reading wrote.
cause: The reading stage builds its plan from the request text. It has no bound on how much machinery a reading may add: a new marker, a fake-runner rig for the caller, display changes. It also has no check that each criterion has the smallest testable seam. The earlier critique's decisions were restated by the user once already (bzw6), and this follow-up still overreached, so the narrowing again came only from the user. The system gives the reading no size or minimality check against one producer run and no carried-over decisions.
prevention: Add a reading-stage check that tests the draft reading before acceptance. (1) Each deliverable has a named, directly testable seam, and test rigs, markers and new states that the design does not need are refused. (2) The total scope fits one producer run. (3) The prior job's recorded critique decisions are attached and must be restated as criteria. A reading that adds a new state, marker or fake-runner rig must justify it against the decisions, or it is cut.
proposed_request: Write landing records to the athena/records branch from gh::land_pr, behind the records sink it already takes. The remote is the source of truth: build the records commit on the remote tip, push with a lease on that tip, move the local ref only after the push succeeds, and on rejection fetch, rebuild and retry a bounded number of times. Test this through the free function gh::land_pr. Add one small constructor that builds the real records sink from a Git and its remote. Athena::land_pr, and so drain.rs, must call it. Test the constructor directly so a test fails if the wiring passes no sink. Do not build a fake-runner rig for Athena::land_pr. Add no merge-requested marker. When the merge cannot be confirmed, write no landing record, print a warning that names the intent, keep today's exit codes, and leave the repair to reconcile (job 3 part 2). Make no display.rs change unless the warning needs one line. Add a CHANGELOG entry.
